::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** [after October 1886][^1]  
**Manuscript:** MS location unknown.  This fragment quoted in Mare and Percival, <i>[Victorian Best-seller](other_books/otherbook_598.qmd)</i>, 228.
:::

Have you heard the last variety of American Lion hunting – writing to ask for a bit of one’s dress to put into a literary quilt?  I actually had such a request, and while I was laughing at it I came on a book of [Miss Alcott](people/person_1649.qmd)’s where the dear Jo – after she had become a noted authoress – has the same entreaty made to her.

---

[^1]: In Jo's Boys, and How They Turned out. A Sequel to "Little Men." (English edition London: Low 1886), 63, a fan asks Jo Bhaer for ‘an old gown or a pair of stockings of yours to put in a rug she’s making’.
